fields.claim_quote: If polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are both unimodal, then $P(x) Q(x)$ is unimodal as well.
fields.explanation: The original P=Q=1+x+3x² are unimodal, while their product coefficients7,6,9 at degrees2,3,4 force a fall followed by a rise. Mathlib Polynomial multiplication/coefficients replace convolution lists. The source theorem does not require symmetric coefficients.
fields.flaw: The product of any two unimodal polynomials is unimodal.
fields.problem: Title: Some families of graphs whose domination polynomials are unimodal
fields.witness: Let P(x)=Q(x)=1+x+3x^2. Each coefficient sequence is (1,1,3), which is nonnegative and weakly increasing, hence unimodal with its mode at degree 2. But P(x)Q(x)=1+2x+7x^2+6x^3+9x^4.
